definitions.explanation: The emergence of a plant sprout or bud from a seed or root.
The first signs or emergence of feelings, ideas, or developments (figurative).

examples.english: In spring, you can see plants sprouting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{種|たね}→種：02157_tane⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{芽生|めば}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}て→出る：00513_deru⟧きた。
⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧⟦{命|いのち}→命：02371_inochi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I feel the budding of new life.

examples.japanese: ⟦{恋|こい}→恋：02208_koi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: I felt the beginning of love.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{正義感|せいぎかん}→正義感：28751_seigikan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あった→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: There was an awakening sense of justice within him.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{好奇心|こうきしん}→好奇心：05213_koukishin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧にしたい。
examples.english: I want to cherish the budding curiosity in children.

notes:
{芽生|めば}え has both a literal botanical meaning (sprouting) and a widely used figurative meaning (the beginning of feelings or ideas).

RELATED VERB:
{芽生|めば}える: to sprout, to bud, to begin to develop

COMMON FIGURATIVE USES:
- ⟦{恋|こい}→恋：02208_koi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え: budding love
- ⟦{希望|きぼう}→希望：00221_kibou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え: budding hope
- ⟦{意識|いしき}→意識：01714_ishiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え: awakening consciousness
- ⟦{好奇心|こうきしん}→好奇心：05213_koukishin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{芽生|めば}え: budding curiosity

USAGE:
The metaphor of a delicate new sprout conveys beginnings that are fragile but full of potential. It is often used in literary and emotional contexts.

RELATED WORDS:

- ⟦{芽|め}→芽：02141_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: to sprout (literal); to start to succeed (figurative)
- ⟦{新芽|しんめ}→新芽：13028_shinme⟧: new shoot/bud
